Preferred
prē-fẽrd´
v. (set before, advanced in rank; rendering Greek emprosthen ginomai, Aramaic netsach, Hebrew shanah)
Latin praeferre, to carry before. The Baptist's Greek is literally that Christ has come to be in front of him — and then the reason, that He was before him.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

John bare witness of Him: “This was he of whom I spake, He that cometh after me is preferred before me: for he was before me” (John 1:15); “He it is, who coming after me is preferred before me, whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose” (John 1:27); “After me cometh a man which is preferred before me: for he was before me” (John 1:30). Daniel “was preferred above the presidents and princes, because an excellent spirit was in him” (Dan 6:3). Hegai “preferred her and her maids unto the best place of the house of the women” (Est 2:9).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines preferred as regarded or valued more; advanced, as to an office or dignity.

expand to see more

PREFERRED, pp. Regarded above others; elevated in estimation; chosen in preference to others; advanced to some office or dignity.

Key Scripture

John 1:15 — "John bare witness of him, and cried, saying, This was he of whom I spake, He that cometh after me is preferred before me: for he was before me."

John 1:30 — "This is he of whom I said, After me cometh a man which is preferred before me: for he was before me."

John 1:27 — "He it is, who coming after me is preferred before me, whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose."

Dan 6:3 — "Then this Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm."

Est 2:9 — "And the maiden pleased him, and she obtained kindness of him; and he speedily gave her her things for purification, with such things as belonged to her, and seven maidens, which were meet to be given her, out of the king's house: and he preferred her and her maids unto the best place of the house of the women."

Modern Corruption

The Baptist's for he was before me is passed over as a courtesy, and it is the pre-existence of the Son from the mouth of a man six months older than He.

expand to see more

John the Baptist was born six months before Jesus, and he said of Jesus, he was before me. The sentence is not deference; it is theology, and the fourth Gospel records it three times so that it cannot be missed. The One who came after John in time was before him in being, because He was in the beginning with God — the prologue of the same chapter — and the Baptist's reason for yielding first place was not that Jesus was greater but that He was earlier than the world. Every denial of the eternal Sonship has to get past a wilderness preacher who understood it. Daniel's preferment is the other kind: an exile advanced over the presidents of Persia because an excellent spirit was in him, and hated for it by men who could find no fault except in the law of his God.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek emprosthen mou gegonen (G1715, G1096), has come to be before me; Aramaic netsach (H5330), to distinguish oneself, be preferred; Hebrew shanah (H8138), to change, advance.

expand to see more

Greek emprosthen mou gegonen (G1715 with G1096) — is preferred before me; John 1:15, 1:27, 1:30.

Aramaic netsach, hithpael (H5330) — to be distinguished, preferred; Daniel 6:3; Hebrew shanah, piel (H8138), Esther 2:9.

Usage

"“Is preferred before me: for he was before me” — the eternal Son, from a man six months older."

"“Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose” — the greatest born of women on his knees."

"“Daniel was preferred above the presidents” — an excellent spirit in an exile."
